source_title: Stop trolling, start introspecting: Congress hits back at PM Modi over MLC poll jibe - India Today
source_excerpt:
Jairam Ramesh said voters across Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had delivered a "no-confidence motion" against PM Modi's policies, asking, "The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's sermonising others!"
The Congress on Thursday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his jibe at the party’s performance in the MLC elections, asking him to stop “trolling” and “sermonising” others and instead reflect on the BJP’s defeat in both seats in his parliamentary constituency of Varanasi.
Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said voters from Varanasi and Nagpur to Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had delivered a “no-confidence motion against” the Prime Minister’s policies.
"The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's sermonising others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?" Ramesh said in his post in Hindi on X.
"Mr. Modi, stop the trolling. Crores of families are reeling from back-breaking inflation, the youth are unemployed, and private investment has ground to a halt," he said.
Ramesh urged the Prime Minister to drop his arrogance and reflect on these issues.
"From Varanasi and Nagpur to Lucknow, Prayagraj, and Patna, the people have clearly passed a no-confidence motion against your policies," the Congress leader said.
The Congress had also hit back at Modi on Wednesday, challenging him to demonstrate his confidence in the BJP’s electoral strength through action rather than rhetoric if he believed electronic voting machines (EVMs) had no bearing on election results.
The party said the Prime Minister should commit to holding all future Lok Sabha and Assembly elections by ballot paper if he was convinced that EVMs did not influence electoral outcomes.
The Congress’s response came after Modi taunted the party over its poor showing in the MLC elections despite the use of paper ballots, a key demand of opposition parties campaigning against EVMs.
The BJP and its NDA allies won 16 of the 28 seats in legislative council elections held across four states. The Congress won one seat, while the Samajwadi Party secured five in Uttar Pradesh, including two in Varanasi.
